item.title: AI Agents
item.description: LLM agents can do a decent first pass at on-call work, but everything they read during an incident is untrusted input. These posts are about giving agents real access to infrastructure while keeping what they can do limited by construction, starting with sandboxed alert triage and remediation on Kubernetes.

item.title: Homelab
item.description: My homelab is a small Docker Swarm of ARM boards and an x86 box across two locations, joined over Tailscale, with Portainer deploying every stack from one Git repo. These posts cover how I keep it running without babysitting it, like pinning images by digest and letting a self-hosted Renovate handle updates.

item.title: Kubernetes
item.description: Managed Kubernetes hides most of the machinery, which is fine until something breaks. These posts go below that layer: bootstrapping a cluster by hand on Vagrant VMs to see how certificates, etcd and pod routing fit together, and running ClickHouse as a replicated cluster with the Altinity operator.

item.title: Cloud
item.description: Most of my day job is on Google Cloud, so this is where I work through AWS and other providers. Free tiers run out quickly, so a lot of it happens against local emulators, starting with why I moved from LocalStack to Floci for testing Terraform.

item.title: Observability
item.description: Notes from keeping monitoring working across many Kubernetes clusters, starting with the move from a federated Prometheus setup that kept running out of memory to Grafana Mimir, without losing historical data.
